englishSourceNotes: 'I can color in the lines': rendered as 'Osaan värittää siististi' — the Finnish esiopetus idiom for colouring without going over the lines; a literal 'viivojen sisälle' is long (31) and clumsy.
'I can catch a fish' → 'Osaan ongella' (the cue is a rod = onki). Catching a fish depends on luck, not skill; 'ongella' is the real yes/no a Finnish child answers.
'I can go on a hike' → 'Osaan retkeillä': 'going on' a hike is not a skill in Finnish; retkeillä is.
'I can help bake a cake' → 'Osaan auttaa leipomisessa' (cake dropped: the cue shows an adult baker with pastries, not a cake).
'I can water the plants' → 'kastella kukat': 5-year-olds say kukat for house plants; 'kasvit' reads as a science word.
'I can swing by myself' → 'keinua ilman apua' (without help = without a push); 'keinua itse' would echo 'pukeutua itse' on another sheet and is ambiguous.

In Finnish 'rapu' is the freshwater crayfish; the picture is a sea crab = 'taskurapu'.
Finnish pannukakku is the oven-baked sheet pancake; a stack of small thick pancakes is 'letut' / 'lätyt' to a Finnish child. Word is understandable but mismatches the picture.
A long knitted winter scarf is 'kaulaliina' (or kaulahuivi); 'huivi' first suggests a headscarf/shawl. Minor.

otherNotes: SELF SHEET VERB CLASH: shipped brushteeth = 'Osaan pestä hampaat' and new washhands = 'Osaan pestä käteni' both use 'pestä'. Recommend changing the shipped brushteeth to 'Osaan harjata hampaani' (equally natural, 21 chars); washhands keeps pestä, which is the only natural verb for hands.
Shipped 'Osaan hyppiä narua' is correct Finnish for jump rope — no change needed (the en 'skip' fix does not affect fi).

farm heading: 'Lempikotieläimeni' — kotieläin is the Finnish esiopetus term for farm animals (kotieläinpiha, maatilan kotieläimet). 'Lempieläimeni maatilalla' is 24 chars, over target. Pets and farm never share a sheet.
pet heading 'Lempilemmikkini' has the lempi/lemmikki sound echo; it is grammatical and children enjoy it. Alternative if disliked: 'Lempilemmikkieläimeni' (21).
bug heading uses 'ötökkä', which in Finnish covers insects, spiders, snails and worms — exactly the row's content.
All headings are single compound words ending in the 1st-person possessive -ni, matching the shipped Lempieläimeni/Lempiruokani; longest 18 characters, no word over 20.
All 27 sentences follow the shipped 'Osaan + infinitive' pattern, ≤ 28 characters, no digits, no braces; no verb repeats within any sheet except the flagged pestä (via shipped string).
